Comment:
Cat A:  Estimated $508,000 for debris removal activities for 26 sites/areas.  The City removed vegetative debris, sediment, rocks, and other disaster debris from public ROWs, trails, public property, drainage channels, culverts and bridges.  Applicant included 2 sites for $300,000 for flooding damage to First Lutheran Church and Washington Elementary School.  These are separate entities.  Creating additional applicant entries in Chart A for the PNP and School District. Reduced: $300,000 for flood damages to school and pnp.  Validated: $208,000 based on debris photos, locations and cost summaries.  
Cat B:  Estimated $7,995 for costs related sandbagging, floodfighting, EOC and other emergency measures.  Validated: $7,995 based on descriptions and cost summaries.
Cat C:  Estimated $1,499,800 for road washouts, sinkholes, culvert failures, ditch damages, shoulder washouts, embankment erosion, riprap washout, road drainage damage and road sign damages across the City.  Applicant submitted 34 damage sites (removed 5 from the iniital submission of 39 sites during PDA).  Reduced: $800,000 for Ruger Ave and Palmer Drive Bridge  because the roads are federal-aid roads and ineligible for PA. Validated: $699,800 based on photos and summaries provided.  
Cat D: Estimated: $1,755,000 for various damages to drainage facilities including washout of riprap and embankment protections, culvert failures, outfall damages, storm sewer pipe damages, blocked/plugged culverts and intake structures and erosion.  Included in this estimate is $500,000 estimated damages to Greenbelt Drainage System (engineered system of channels, basins, outfalls, culverts, etc) and $1,000,000 estimated for debris and shoreline damages to Springbrook and Blackhawk Creeks.  Conducted site visits to Greenbelt and Springbrook and Blackhawk Creeks, and Applicnat provided detailed damage photos for remaining sites.  Site visits showed major washouts around culverts, trails, and gabion baskets along creek, and significant vegetative debris blocking channels and culverts. Reduced: $700,000 for shoreline grading, seeding and stabilization along Springbrook and Blackhawk Creeks.  Site visits showed mostly unimproved embankments and natural land, without evidence of maintained improvements.  Able to validate debris blocking creeks and inlets, and damage to existing gabion baskets.  Also able to validate damages to Greenbelt through site visits.  Validated: $1,055,000 based on photos, site inspections and cost summaries.  
Cat E: Estimated: $7,015,000 for flood damage to 4 buildings: Washington Elementary School, First Lutheran Church, Janesville Fire Training Center and City Building.  Washington Elementary School is responsibility of Janesville School District, not the City and First Lutheran Church is responsibility of PNP.  Reduced: $7,000,000 for the school and PNP damages and addressing those costs under their own separate applicant entries on the Chart A. Validated: $15,000 for city building and fire training center based on photos and cost summaries.
Cat F: Estimated: $6,539,600 for damages to City's storm sewer system; increased sewage treatment costs; and traffic light signal damages.  Applicant estimating 40% of storm sewer system needs to be cleaned of debris and 90% of the outfalls need clearance and repairs. City just completed its annual storm sewer cleaning and based estimates for cleaning on those maintenance contracts.  Conducted site visits on a sampling of outfalls and inlets from all areas of the City. Outfalls showing massive washout damages and vegetative and sediment debris throughout the pipes we sampled. Inlets similarly show visible vegetative and sediment debris in pipes. The Applicant estimating an average of $5,000 of debris and repair work per outfall. CEFs completed for a couple of the sites visited, showed damages and costs to those would be significantly higher. Thus, the low average estimate of $5,000 is reasonable. Reduced:  $1,320,000 for number of outfalls to be repaired.  Removed approximately 300 outfalls from original estimate of 930 based on GIS mapping and discussions with the Applicant and State regarding areas of city impacted and legal responsibility.  Reduced: $3,600 for increased operating costs of having to treat more gallons of water than typical due to flooding.  These increased costs not tied to eligible emergency protective measure, just increased usage of its normal service.  Validated: $5,216,000 based on system maps, photos, site visits, and cost estimates based on historical costs.  
Cat G: Estimated: $850,000 for 26 park sites, including trail washouts, walking bridge damages and other park washouts. Reduced: $75,000 for road damages claimed to site 51451 (Cemetery Road) because damage photos show signifcant alligator cracking, potholes and prior deterioration.  Validated: $775,000 based on photos, site visits and cost summaries.
